1. Intro to Microeconomics

First steps in microeconomics — no calculus, learn by touching sliders. From gasoline prices and lunch menus to cafes, subscriptions, and cigarette taxes: see the logic behind everyday choices.

  • Where Demand Meets Supply — Touch why a liter of gasoline costs what it costs. Quantity demanded Qd=a−bPQ_d = a - bPQd​=a−bP falls as price rises; quantity supplied Qs=dPQ_s = dPQs​=dP rises. The point where the two match — Qd=QsQ_d = Q_sQd​=Qs​ — is the equilibrium.
  • Splitting the Lunch Budget — Split a 404040 lunch budget between two foods. The money constraint is one line: p1x1+p2x2=mp_1 x_1 + p_2 x_2 = mp1​x1​+p2​x2​=m. The best combo is where the last won buys the same happiness everywhere — raise a price and watch that point slide.
  • The Cafe Owner's Math — You run a cafe. The cost of one more cup is MC=ΔC/ΔqMC = \Delta C / \Delta qMC=ΔC/Δq — rising with every cup. While the price PPP beats that cost, selling pays; stopping at P=MCP = MCP=MC is the answer.
  • Competition vs Monopoly — The same streaming market, side by side: competition left, monopoly right. The monopolist stops at MR=MCMR = MCMR=MC, and the lost triangle (deadweight loss) glows red. Lower the demand responsiveness and the red triangle grows — insensitive customers hurt more.
  • Taxes and Price Ceilings — Who pays a 333 cigarette tax? The tax wedge Pb=Ps+tP_b = P_s + tPb​=Ps​+t lands heavier on the side that cannot walk away. A rent ceiling, meanwhile, freezes the price but creates a queue. Push the sliders and see for yourself.
